context: This scenario tests whether the evaluatee correctly uses the package to intercept and log direct property mutations on tracked objects. The key behaviors are: the logger is called with the correct violation type (FORGET_MUTATE_IMMUT), source, key, and new value; and the write still takes effect so the object remains usable. Criteria focus exclusively on package API usage.

checklist.name: Apply tracking
checklist.description: buildMakeReadOnly is called with the logger and the returned makeReadOnly function is applied to the object before any mutations occur.

checklist.name: Logger called on write
checklist.description: After tracking is applied, a direct property write triggers the logger with the FORGET_MUTATE_IMMUT violation type as the first argument.

checklist.name: Logger receives key and value
checklist.description: The logger is called with the mutated property key (third argument) and the new value (fourth argument).

checklist.name: Write takes effect
checklist.description: After the violation is logged, reading the mutated property returns the new value, demonstrating that the write succeeded in the package's internal backing store.
